Get or set names of columns that contain IMU data in a move2

Source: R/imu_col_attr.R
mt_imu_column.Rd

Designate columns in a move2 object that contain a given class of IMU data. This allows you to flexibly store IMU data produced by as_acc(), as_mag(), or as_gyro() in a column in a move2 and access it programmatically, without needing to hard-code column names.

  • mt_*_column() returns the name of the column in the input move2 that contains data from the indicated sensor.

  • mt_set_*_column() sets the column that contains data from the indicated sensor.

Usage

mt_acc_column(x)

mt_mag_column(x)

mt_gyro_column(x)

mt_set_acc_column(x, value)

mt_set_mag_column(x, value)

mt_set_gyro_column(x, value)

Arguments

x

A move2 object with an IMU vector column (for instance, produced by as_acc(), as_mag(), or as_gyro()).

value

A string giving the name of the column in x that contains the extracted IMU data. The column must contain a vector of the corresponding sensor type (e.g. acc).

Value

mt_*_column() returns a length-one character vector naming the designated column.

mt_set_*_column() returns x with the corresponding attribute set to value.

Details

These functions behave similarly to move2's native helpers (e.g. move2::mt_time_column()). They work by storing a character attribute in the input move2 object naming the relevant column of IMU data.

Save your data to RDS (e.g. with saveRDS()) so the attributes are kept when data are loaded again.

Current limitations

The stored column name is an ordinary attribute of the move2, so it is not always kept when the data are modified.

For instance, some common data manipulation operations drop these attributes, like dplyr::distinct(), dplyr::summarize(), dplyr::ungroup(), grouped dplyr::mutate(), and move2::mt_stack(). This behavior depends on how lower-level packages like sf and move2 handle these attributes, so many of these discrepancies may be resolved in the future.

Further, renaming the column (e.g. with dplyr::rename()) does not update the attribute simultaneously, which can create a mismatch between the stored column name and the name of the column in the data themselves. Use mt_set_*_column() to update the column name accordingly.

See also

mt_acc(), mt_mag(), mt_gyro() to extract the column values.

as_acc(), as_mag(), as_gyro() to build IMU columns.

Examples

alb <- albatrosses()
alb$acc <- as_acc(alb)
alb <- mt_set_acc_column(alb, "acc")

mt_acc_column(alb)
#> [1] "acc"

mt_acc(alb)[1:10]
#> <acceleration[10]>
#>  [1] <NA>              (1824.17 1913.83) (1904.3 1926.5)   (1823.27 1913.42)
#>  [5] (1826.7 1915.7)   (1719.07 1908.8)  <NA>              (1943.47 2028.05)
#>  [9] (1927.98 2013.72) (1926.7 2008.82) 
#> # frequency: 5 [Hz]
